title: Customer replay kit + evidence package for output regression (customer-facing draft)
body:
Summary (customer-facing top‑line):

We identified a regression that caused intermittent changes in generated output quality for a subset of tenant requests between 2029-11-29 03:40 UTC and 2029-11-29 07:05 UTC. For impacted customers we are offering a guided replay kit so you and our team can reproduce, validate, and if desired, re-generate affected responses. This note contains: a short timeline, a plain‑language root cause, what we have done already, and a step‑by-step replay + evidence package customers can use to work with us.

Short status page blurb (3 lines, for status.redwood.ai):
- Incident: Intermittent output regressions affecting a small percentage of requests in EU region.
- Impact window: 2029-11-29 03:40 UTC — 2029-11-29 07:05 UTC.
- Current status: Stabilized; guided replay available for customers who need re-generation or verification.

Customer-facing post-incident summary (concise):
- Scope: ~0.8% of total tokens served in eu-west-1 during the window were associated with model execution paths that produced altered completions (duplicates, truncation, or slightly altered phrasing). Not a data leak or corruption.
- Root cause (plain language): A recently rolled kernel optimization for a quantized model variant produced slightly different token selection probabilities under a narrow sequence-length + attention pattern. The optimization was intended to improve throughput but introduced a subtle numerical shift for long prompt prefixes.
- What we did: rolled back the kernel change for the affected pool within 25 minutes of detection, added a per-model Canary run, and invalidated the affected runtime cache. We also disabled the aggressive kernel selection heuristic while we investigate.

Replay kit and evidence package (what we offer customers):
Purpose: enable customers to reproduce the exact server-side inference that produced the original output (for auditing, re-generation, or verification). The kit is intentionally minimal and safe — it does not require sharing sensitive user content unless you choose to.

1) What to collect (customer checklist):
- Affected request IDs (token: request_id) or example request timestamps in UTC.
- Tenant ID / project key.
- The prompt(s) or a redacted version (if you cannot share full PII). If redacting, keep token boundaries if possible.
- Model name + model_version reported in logs (e.g., open-64b@v2029-11-18).
- Sequence length and any function-call / streaming flags.
- SDK or curl client version and any non-default headers.
- If available: trace_id / span_id from the request trace.

2) How to export logs (suggested customer steps):
- From your app logs: filter by tenant_id and UTC time window.
- If using our client SDKs, run the debug logger: REDWOOD_SDK_LOG=trace and capture the request/response pairs.
- Optional: export the relevant traces from your tracing provider (Jaeger/Datadog) using the trace_id.

3) How to run a safe replay (recommended methods):
- Option A — Local replay (recommended for small sets):
  * Replace any PII in prompt with placeholders.
  * Use the exact model name + model_version from logs.
  * Use the following curl template (replace values):
    curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n      -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \n      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n      -d '{"model":"open-64b@v2029-11-18","input":"<REDACTED_PROMPT>","max_tokens":256,"temperature":0.0,"trace_id":"<TRACE_ID_IF_AVAILABLE>"}'

- Option B — Replay with Redwood assistance (recommended for larger batches or if you want us to re‑generate and attest):
  * Upload an evidence package (see upload instructions below).
  * Provide the list of request_ids or sample prompts and the desired re-generation policy (exact-match / best-effort / temperature-adjusted).
  * We will run replays in an isolated environment using the same runtime config and provide a signed artifact that shows input, output, model version, and runtime checksum.

4) Evidence package format (single compressed archive):
- manifest.txt — list of request_ids, timestamps, model_version, tenant_id.
- requests.csv — one row per request: request_id,timestamp,model,flags,redacted_prompt_hash.
- optional: prompts/ (redacted prompt text files) — include only if you consent.
- optional: traces/ (trace json) — span traces if available.
- checksum.sha256 — sha256 of the package.

5) How to upload securely to Redwood for assisted replay:
- We provide a pre-signed S3 upload link per customer (expires 48h). To request it, open a customer-success ticket with the subject: "Replay package upload request — <tenant_id>" and attach the manifest.
- If you prefer enterprise SFTP or a private connector, tell your CSM and we will arrange it.

6) Re-generation policies we will offer:
- exact-match: attempt to reproduce the original tokens using deterministic settings (temperature=0, seed locked) — note: identical output not guaranteed across quantized kernels but we will provide runtime checksum and seed used.
- best-effort: regenerate with latest stable kernel; chosen when customers prioritize highest semantic fidelity rather than bit-for-bit equality.
- safe-redact: re-generate with PII scrubbed from outputs if requested.

Operational notes for customers (what to expect):
- Turnaround: small packages (<= 200 requests) — 1 business day; large datasets — estimate in ticket.
- Attestation: we will provide a signed report with inputs, model_version, runtime_checksum, and the re‑generated outputs.
- Credits: if you believe your SLAs were impacted materially, include your SLO / billing window and we will route to Billing for a credit review; CSMs can pre-authorize small goodwill credits for verified impacts.

Immediate customer mitigations (recommended):
- If you need guaranteed stable outputs for critical flows, pin to a stable model_version and request dedicated capacity while we finalize kernel validation.
- Add a quick client-side checksum comparison for important responses and trigger an automated re‑query with a different model_version upon mismatch.
- Prefer deterministic settings for audit paths: temperature=0, top_p=1.0, explicit max_tokens.

Internal notes / engineering summary (short):
- Root cause details: optimization adjusted matmul accumulation order for int8 path; under a small set of attention masks and long left-context, rounding behavior altered logits ranking for a tiny fraction of tokens.
- Primary remediation: rollback applied; add long-prefix canaries; add numerical regression tests using fuzzed long-prefix prompts.
- Next engineering steps: 1) implement deterministic fallback for quantized kernels; 2) run an extended A/B with real traffic replays; 3) add model-level flag to opt-out of heuristic kernel selection.

Customer FAQ (anticipated):
Q: Will my user data have been exposed?
A: No — there was no data exfiltration. The issue is numerical divergence in model computation, not a storage or access event.

Q: Can you guarantee exact same outputs if you re-run now?
A: Not always. For exact-match attempts we lock seeds and runtime config; however, quantized kernels may still differ. We will provide runtime checksum and the level of match (byte-for-byte vs semantic).

Q: Do I need to share raw user prompts?
A: No — redacted prompts and hashes are sufficient for triage. If you prefer full prompts for re-generation you can provide them but only via secure upload.

How to request the replay kit from Redwood (customer action):
- Open a support ticket to your CSM or support@redwood.ai with subject: "Request: Replay kit + evidence upload — <tenant_id>" and include manifest.txt (or a short list of request_ids and timestamps).

Contacts:
- CSM: Marcus Liu (marcus@redwood.ai)
- Incident lead: Elena Martinez (elena@redwood.ai)
- Engineering escalation: Priya Desai (priya@redwood.ai)

Open items / TODOs (internal):
- [ ] Draft a short public status page blurb for the domain team to post. (Owner: Elena)
- [ ] Confirm S3 pre-signed upload flow and template email (Owner: SRE ops)
- [ ] Add a canned script that verifies runtime_checksum and produces attestation (Owner: Runtime eng)

Notes to reviewer: this is a hybrid customer-facing / internal playbook. Keep the top portion (Summary, blurb, short post-incident) customer-friendly. The replay steps are actionable but can be simplified further for non-technical accounts. Feedback welcome on: wording for upload security, credit policy phrase, and the exact SLA turnaround language.

End of draft.
